entry.title: Ff159 WebGL ext EXT_clip_control and EXT_texture_mirror_clamp_to_edge
entry.content:
FF159 adds support for EXT_clip_control and EXT_texture_mirror_clamp_to_edge in WebGL1.0 and 2 in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1885031 and https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1908749

Tests

  • https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/sdk/tests/conformance/extensions/ext-clip-control.html
  • https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/sdk/tests/conformance/extensions/ext-texture-mirror-clamp-to-edge.html

Related docs work can be tracked in:

  • mdn/content#46145
  • mdn/content#46146

The versions for these are given by Claude as below in details. Then verified using above tests.

Details

Chrome

Both extensions landed in September 2023 as draft extensions. Drafts are only exposed when the WebGL Draft
Extensions flag is turned on. I found the commits that removed that requirement and mapped them to Chrome
versions with chromiumdash:

  • : Chrome 122. It was first promoted in November 2023, but that was reverted before the
    Chrome 121 branch point, so it never shipped in 121. It was promoted again in January 2024 (0c83005fec,
    first in 122.0.6260.0; the 122 branch point is 6261).
  • EXT_texture_mirror_clamp_to_edge: Chrome 124. It was promoted in February 2024 (f8dd44d6d3, first in
    124.0.6317.0; the 123 branch point is 6312).
  • EXT_polygon_offset_clamp was promoted in the same commit as EXT_clip_control, and BCD already lists it as
    Chrome 122 / Safari 17.4. That backs up the 122 result.
  • chromestatus: No entries. Searches for both names on the chromestatus API return nothing. Chrome usually
    doesn't create chromestatus entries for individual WebGL extensions.

Safari

Both extensions landed in WebKit in August 2023, also gated on draft extensions. I checked the code on
WebKit's Safari release branches:

  • EXT_clip_control: Safari 17.4. It moved out of draft in WebKit commit dbf64f1b24, the commit Bugzilla links
    from Firefox bug 1885031, and is enabled on the 17.4 branch. The Safari 17.4 release post confirms it:
    "WebKit for Safari 17.4 adds support for four new WebGL extensions: EXT_clip_control, EXT_depth_clamp,
    EXT_polygon_offset_clamp, and WEBGL_polygon_mode."
  • EXT_texture_mirror_clamp_to_edge: Safari 18.0. It moved out of draft in WebKit commit e65977cbea
    (January 2024), but that change didn't reach the 17.x branches. It still requires draft extensions on the
    17.4, 17.5 and 17.6 branches and is enabled only on the 18.0 branch.
  • Release notes: The posts for 17.4 and 17.5 don't mention mirror clamp. I didn't check the Safari 18.0 post
    because you rejected that fetch, so 18.0 rests on the branch code alone.

entry.title: fix: correct Chrome break avoidance support
entry.content:
Summary

  • Update Chrome support for break-before: avoid-page to Chrome 108.
  • Update Chrome support for break-after: avoid-page to Chrome 108, including its paged_context entry.

Additional details

  • Chrome 108 release notes document printing support for the avoid value of break-before, break-after, and break-inside as part of LayoutNG printing.
  • Chromium's LayoutNG printing test updates also confirm that break avoidance requested by break-before and break-after is supported.
  • Based on this evidence, Chrome's version_added value is updated to 108 for avoid-page under break-before and break-after, including the break-after paged_context entry.

Closes #15255

entry.title: Rename nested `@page` at-rules
entry.content:
Summary

Rename ids to remove the "at_" prefix from nested @page at-rules.

This was only recently introduced in #30612. I should have insisted on removing all prefixed ids in my review...

At-rules generally have no "at_" prefix. Not the general ones, but also not the nested ones (nesting happens in @page and in @font-feature-values). We should either have the prefix everywhere or nowhere. Since at-rules never had a prefix, I'm removing this newly introduced prefix.

Also, as of openwebdocs/mdn-bcd-collector#3477, the Collector can test support for at-rules and relies on consistent BCD paths.

Test results and supporting details

Data is the same. The linter reordered the data.

Related issues

#30612

entry.title: css(outline-offset): add `inset` keyword value
entry.content:
Adds css.properties.outline-offset.inset for the inset keyword value of outline-offset, which draws the outline inside the element's border edge.

Browser support

  • Safari 27 (2026-09-14): first stable release
  • All other browsers: not yet shipped

Additional Details

  • WebKit commit a69b24040c7a, bug 317779, landed 2026-07-07
  • STP 249 release notes explicitly list "Added support for outline-offset: inset" (released 2026-07-29, after Safari 26.6 on 2026-07-27 — so 26.6 does not include it)
  • Spec tracking: CSSWG issue #13765 (css-ui-4 not yet updated; spec_url points to #outline-offset in the interim)
  • WPT: PR #60879

Related issue:

mdn/content#45043

entry.title: Mirror legacy Edge statements from Chromium
entry.content:
Summary

Mirror Edge 79+ support from Chromium for legacy-only Edge statements, so Chrome's notes, partial implementation, and removals apply to Edge 79+. Built output is unchanged. Adds an internal mirror: false opt-out and marks 241 features for review.

Test results and supporting details

  • Unit suite passes (371 tests).
  • Built data is byte-identical to main.
  • Data changes are limited to "mirror": false markers: 254 statements across 241 features. Reviewers can list every opt-out by searching for the flag.
  • Continuous support stays a single statement. A second statement appears only where the Chromium-era data differs.

entry.title: Add FontFace.sizeAdjust compatibility data
entry.content:
Summary

Add compatibility data for FontFace.sizeAdjust, the JavaScript property corresponding to the @font-face size-adjust descriptor. Record Chrome 92, Firefox 92, and Safari 17, with derived browsers mirrored.

Test results and supporting details

  • npm test passed: formatting/type checks, data lint, and all 347 unit tests.
  • Reviewed the final diff separately and checked implementation/release evidence:
    • Chromium 92 FontFace IDL gates the property on CSSFontFaceSizeAdjust. The flag changes from test in 91 to stable in 92.
    • Gecko bug 1698495 includes the WebIDL implementation; the shipping announcement identifies Firefox 92 as the default-enabled release.
    • WebKit implementation commit adds the FontFace property and constructor descriptor and enables the shared feature flag. Safari 17 release notes confirm the shipping release.
  • The current specification includes sizeAdjust in FontFace's IDL, but has no dedicated property anchor, so this links to the interface section.
  • Omit mdn_url until the accompanying reference page is published.

Related issues

Related to mdn/content#36587. This is the BCD-first change requested in mdn/content#36587 (comment); documentation follows separately.

entry.title: Note that forced-colors: active is never true in Safari
entry.content:
Summary

Adds a Safari note to css.at-rules.media.forced-colors: forced-colors: active is never true, as Apple platforms have no forced colors mode, and the feature always matches forced-colors: none. Safari on iOS inherits it through mirror. Same shape as the display-mode: minimal-ui notes in the same file.

Test results and supporting details

WebKit implemented the feature as a placeholder that always matches none because Cocoa has no forced colors concept: bug 225281, landed as 253290@main for Safari 16. The issue reporter confirmed that Increase Contrast on macOS does not apply rules inside @media (forced-colors: active).

Chrome Android and Firefox Android, raised in the issue, are left out: their behaviour was not verified here and can follow in a separate PR.

node lint/lint.js css/at-rules/media.json: all data passed linting.

Related issues

Fixes #27143

entry.title: Add navigation and types descriptors to @view-transition
entry.content:
Summary

Adds css.at-rules.view-transition.navigation and css.at-rules.view-transition.types, the two descriptors of the @view-transition rule, with the same support as the at-rule: Chrome 126, Safari 18.2, Firefox unsupported, the rest mirrored. The entries follow the shape of other at-rule descriptors such as @property and carry no mdn_url, since MDN has no page for either descriptor yet.

Test results and supporting details

Spec: navigation and types in CSS View Transitions 2.
Chromium: @view-transition parses only when ViewTransitionOnNavigation is enabled, stable in 126 (chromestatus); types was already in CSSViewTransitionRule.idl at 126.0.6478.0.
WebKit: types descriptor added in bug 278000 (282221@main), the at-rule with cross-document view transitions in bug 278247, both released in Safari 18.2.
WPT: css/css-view-transitions/navigation/at-rule-opt-in-auto.html and css/css-view-transitions/navigation/with-types/at-rule-with-types-parsing.html.
node lint/lint.js css/at-rules/view-transition.json: all data passed linting.

Related issues

Fixes #25573

entry.title: fix(html): add notes for dialog closedby=any touch propagation bug
entry.content:
Fixes #30474

<dialog closedby="any"> has a touch event propagation bug in Chrome 134–153
and Firefox 141+: tapping the backdrop closes the dialog but does not cancel
the event, causing click listeners on elements behind the backdrop to fire.

Changes:

  • Chrome: converted to array — clean entry for 154+ (fixed via
    bug 425579196), plus a 134–153 entry with a note
  • Firefox: added notes to the 141+ entry linking to
    bug 2022750 (still unfixed as of Firefox 156)
  • chrome_android, edge, and firefox_android correctly mirror their
    desktop entries — no additional changes needed

entry.title: html/elements/iframe: add local-network, local-network-access, and loopback-network allow directives
entry.content:
Fixes #30831

Adds three missing Permission Policy directive entries to html.elements.iframe.allow:

  • local-network: Chrome 145, Firefox 153, experimental: false
  • loopback-network: Chrome 145, Firefox 153, experimental: false
  • local-network-access: Chrome 142, Firefox false, experimental: true (legacy alias, superseded by the two above)

Firefox support verified via Bugzilla bug 1978550 (RESOLVED FIXED); network.lna.blocking defaults to true from the Firefox 153 release tag.

Note: http.headers.Permissions-Policy entries for these directives correctly remain false — Firefox has not implemented HTTP header parsing for Permissions-Policy (bug 1531012 is still open).
